userStories.title: User Registration with Email and Password
userStories.description: As a new user, I want to register with email and password so I can create an account and access Rorcha's platform features.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/auth/register accepts email, password, and displayName fields and creates a new user row in the users table
Passwords are hashed with bcrypt (cost factor 12) before storage — plaintext never persisted
Registration returns 409 if email already exists with error message 'Email already registered'
Email validation rejects malformed addresses and returns 400 with specific validation error
Successful registration returns 201 with JWT access token and refresh token in response body

userStories.title: JWT Session Management with Refresh Tokens
userStories.description: As an authenticated user, I want my sessions managed via JWT tokens with automatic refresh so I stay logged in without frequent re-authentication.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/auth/login returns a short-lived access token (15 min) and long-lived refresh token (7 days) as JSON
POST /api/auth/refresh accepts a valid refresh token and returns a new access/refresh token pair, invalidating the old refresh token
Expired access tokens return 401 with error 'Token expired' — frontend intercepts and attempts silent refresh
Refresh tokens are stored in a refresh_tokens table with user_id, token_hash, expires_at, and revoked_at columns
POST /api/auth/logout revokes the refresh token by setting revoked_at timestamp

userStories.title: GitHub OAuth Authentication
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to sign in with my GitHub account so I can authenticate quickly and link my GitHub identity for later integration features.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/auth/github redirects to GitHub OAuth authorization URL with correct client_id and scope (user:email, repo)
GET /api/auth/github/callback exchanges the authorization code for a GitHub access token and creates or links a user account
If a user with the same GitHub email already exists, the accounts are linked rather than creating a duplicate
GitHub access token is encrypted at rest in a github_connections table with user_id, github_user_id, encrypted_token, and scopes columns
Login via GitHub returns the same JWT access/refresh token pair as email login

userStories.title: Authentication Middleware and Route Protection
userStories.description: As a platform operator, I want all API routes protected by authentication middleware so only authenticated users can access platform resources.
acceptanceCriteria: An authRequired middleware function extracts and verifies the JWT from the Authorization: Bearer header
Protected routes return 401 with error 'Authentication required' when no token is provided
The middleware attaches req.user with id, email, and role fields for downstream route handlers
Public routes (/api/auth/*, /api/health) are explicitly excluded from authentication
Invalid or malformed tokens return 401 with error 'Invalid token'

userStories.title: Database Schema: Users, Teams, and Roles
userStories.description: As a platform developer, I want the database schema extended with users, teams, and role tables so multi-user and team features have a data foundation.
acceptanceCriteria: Migration creates users table with id, email, password_hash, display_name, avatar_url, github_user_id, created_at, updated_at columns
Migration creates teams table with id, name, slug, owner_id (FK users), created_at columns
Migration creates team_members table with team_id, user_id, role (admin/editor/viewer), invited_at, accepted_at columns
Migration creates workspace_access table linking workspace_id to team_id with permission level
All foreign keys have ON DELETE CASCADE and indexes exist on lookup columns (email, team_id, user_id)

userStories.title: Login and Registration UI Components
userStories.description: As a user, I want a polished login and registration page so I can authenticate through an intuitive interface.
acceptanceCriteria: LoginPage component renders email/password fields, a 'Sign in' button, and a 'Sign in with GitHub' OAuth button
RegisterPage component renders email, password, confirm password, and display name fields with client-side validation
Form validation shows inline errors for mismatched passwords, invalid email format, and password minimum length (8 chars)
Successful login redirects to the dashboard and stores tokens in memory (not localStorage for XSS safety)
AuthContext provider wraps the app and exposes user, login, logout, and isAuthenticated state

userStories.title: Mermaid Diagram Generation in Spec Output
userStories.description: As a developer, I want specs to include auto-generated Mermaid dependency diagrams so I can visualize story relationships at a glance.
acceptanceCriteria: The spec generation prompt instructs the LLM to produce a mermaidDiagram field containing a valid Mermaid flowchart of story dependencies
The mermaidDiagram string is stored in the spec JSON alongside userStories and returned by GET /api/specs/:id
Frontend renders the Mermaid diagram using mermaid.js in the spec detail view with zoom and pan controls
Stories with no dependencies appear as root nodes; dependency edges use the story ID labels
A 'Copy Mermaid' button copies the raw diagram source to clipboard for use in documentation

userStories.title: Inline Story Editing with AI Rewrite
userStories.description: As a spec author, I want to click on any story in a pending spec and edit it inline with an AI-assisted rewrite option so I can refine individual stories without regenerating the entire spec.
acceptanceCriteria: Clicking a story card in the spec detail view opens an inline edit form with title, description, and acceptance criteria fields
A 'Rewrite with AI' button sends the current story plus user instructions to the LLM and replaces the fields with the AI response
PUT /api/specs/:specId/stories/:storyId updates a single story within the spec JSON on disk and bumps the spec version
Editing a story creates a new spec_versions entry preserving the pre-edit state
The inline editor supports Markdown preview for the description field

userStories.title: Story Complexity Scoring
userStories.description: As a project manager, I want each story to have an AI-estimated complexity score so I can prioritize and plan sprint capacity.
acceptanceCriteria: During spec generation, each story receives a complexity field with value 1-5 (1=trivial, 5=epic) based on acceptance criteria count and description analysis
GET /api/specs/:id returns stories with their complexity scores included
The spec detail UI shows complexity as a colored badge (green=1-2, yellow=3, red=4-5) on each story card
A summary bar at the top of the spec shows total complexity points and average complexity
Manual override of complexity is supported via PUT /api/specs/:specId/stories/:storyId with a complexity field

userStories.title: Spec Readiness Percentage Calculator
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to see a readiness percentage for each spec so I know how close it is to being fully implementable.
acceptanceCriteria: Readiness is calculated as: (stories with >=3 acceptance criteria AND no unresolved dependencies) / total stories * 100
GET /api/specs/:id includes a readinessPercent field in the response
The spec list view shows a progress ring or bar displaying the readiness percentage for each spec
Stories flagged as 'not ready' are highlighted with a warning icon and tooltip explaining what's missing
Readiness recalculates automatically when stories are edited or dependencies change

userStories.title: Bulk Story Operations
userStories.description: As a spec manager, I want to select multiple stories and perform bulk actions (exclude, delete, move, re-order) so I can manage large specs efficiently.
acceptanceCriteria: A checkbox appears on each story card; a 'Select All' toggle selects/deselects all visible stories
A bulk action toolbar appears when stories are selected with options: Exclude, Include, Delete, and Set Priority
POST /api/specs/:specId/stories/bulk accepts an action and array of storyIds and applies the operation atomically
Bulk delete removes stories from the spec JSON and reindexes remaining story IDs to maintain sequential order
All bulk operations create a spec_versions entry for undo capability

userStories.title: Spec Tagging System
userStories.description: As a user, I want to tag specs with custom labels so I can organize and filter my spec library by project area, priority, or any custom taxonomy.
acceptanceCriteria: Migration creates a spec_tags table with spec_id, tag_name, and created_at columns with unique constraint on (spec_id, tag_name)
POST /api/specs/:id/tags adds one or more tags to a spec; DELETE /api/specs/:id/tags/:tag removes a tag
GET /api/specs accepts a tags query parameter that filters results to specs matching all specified tags
The spec card UI shows tags as colored chips; clicking a tag filters the list to that tag
An autocomplete dropdown suggests existing tags when adding new ones to maintain consistency

userStories.title: Spec Forking and Duplication
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to fork an existing spec to create an independent copy so I can experiment with variations without modifying the original.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/specs/:id/fork creates a deep copy of the spec with a new slug (original-slug-fork-N) and resets all passes to false
The forked spec includes a forkedFrom field referencing the original spec ID for traceability
Forked specs appear in the spec list with a fork icon badge showing their origin
The fork operation preserves all stories, tags, and direction layer associations from the original
Users can optionally provide a new title and brief when forking via request body parameters

userStories.title: Cross-Spec Story Search
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to search for stories across all specs in my workspace so I can find related work, avoid duplication, and reference existing implementations.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/stories/search accepts a query parameter and searches story titles, descriptions, and acceptance criteria across all specs
Results include the parent spec ID, spec title, and workspace name for each matching story
Search supports filtering by spec status (pending/approved/archived), workspace, and tags
Results are paginated with items array, total count, and hasMore boolean
Response time is under 200ms for workspaces with up to 1000 total stories

userStories.title: Parallel Story Execution Engine
userStories.description: As a pipeline operator, I want stories without mutual dependencies to execute in parallel across multiple Claude instances so pipeline runs complete faster.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/pipeline/trigger accepts a parallelism parameter (1-5) controlling the maximum concurrent Claude invocations
The execution engine builds a dependency DAG and identifies stories that can run concurrently at each level
Each parallel story runs in its own git worktree branch to prevent file conflicts
WAL events include a worker_id field so the UI can show which stories are running on which worker
If a story fails, dependent stories are automatically skipped with status 'blocked' and reason referencing the failed dependency

userStories.title: Story Queue Prioritization
userStories.description: As a pipeline manager, I want to set execution priority on stories so critical path items run first when parallelism is constrained.
acceptanceCriteria: Each story supports a priority field (1=urgent, 2=high, 3=normal, 4=low) defaulting to 3
PUT /api/specs/:specId/stories/:storyId accepts a priority field to update story priority
The execution engine sorts runnable stories by priority (ascending) before assigning to workers
The pipeline monitor UI shows priority badges on queued stories and allows drag-to-reorder
Priority changes during an active run take effect for stories not yet started

userStories.title: Custom Timeout Per Story
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to set custom timeouts on individual stories so long-running infrastructure stories don't get killed prematurely while keeping short stories from hanging.
acceptanceCriteria: Each story supports a timeoutMinutes field (5-120, default 45) in the spec JSON
The pipeline engine passes the story-specific timeout to gtimeout when spawning the Claude process
PUT /api/specs/:specId/stories/:storyId accepts timeoutMinutes to update the timeout
When a story times out, it's marked as 'timeout' status in story_results with the actual elapsed time recorded
The spec detail UI shows timeout settings inline with a quick-edit number input

userStories.title: Pipeline Pre/Post Hooks
userStories.description: As a DevOps engineer, I want to configure shell commands that run before and after pipeline execution so I can integrate with external systems like test suites and deployment scripts.
acceptanceCriteria: Migration creates a pipeline_hooks table with workspace_id, hook_type (pre_run/post_run/pre_story/post_story), command, and enabled columns
POST /api/pipeline/hooks creates a new hook; PUT updates; DELETE removes by ID
Pre-run hooks execute before the first story and abort the run if any hook exits non-zero
Post-run hooks execute after the last story with RUN_STATUS and RUN_ID environment variables available
Hook stdout/stderr is captured and appended to the run's terminal output buffer

userStories.title: Dry-Run with Cost Estimate
userStories.description: As a cost-conscious developer, I want to dry-run a pipeline to see an estimated token cost before committing to execution so I can budget appropriately.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/pipeline/trigger with dryRun=true returns a cost estimate without starting any Claude processes
The estimate calculates input tokens based on direction stack size + story prompt size using a token counting heuristic (chars/4)
Output token estimate uses historical average from story_results of similar complexity scores
Cost is calculated using configurable per-model rates stored in a model_pricing table (input_cost_per_1k, output_cost_per_1k)
The dry-run response includes per-story breakdown and total estimated cost in USD

userStories.title: Pipeline Scheduling with Cron
userStories.description: As a team lead, I want to schedule pipeline runs on a cron schedule so specs can be executed automatically during off-hours.
acceptanceCriteria: Migration creates a pipeline_schedules table with workspace_id, spec_id, cron_expression, enabled, and last_triggered_at columns
POST /api/pipeline/schedules creates a schedule; cron expression is validated using cron-parser library
A background scheduler checks for due schedules every 60 seconds and triggers pipeline runs
GET /api/pipeline/schedules lists all schedules with next_run_at calculated from the cron expression
Scheduled runs appear in pipeline_runs with trigger_type='scheduled' to distinguish from manual triggers

userStories.title: Interactive Dependency DAG Visualization
userStories.description: As a developer, I want an interactive SVG dependency graph in the pipeline monitor so I can see story execution flow, status, and critical path in real-time.
acceptanceCriteria: The pipeline monitor renders a DAG using dagre-d3 or similar library with stories as nodes and dependencies as directed edges
Node colors reflect real-time status: gray=pending, blue=running, green=passed, red=failed, yellow=skipped
Clicking a node opens a popover showing the story title, current status, elapsed time, and log tail
The critical path (longest dependency chain) is highlighted with a thicker edge style
The DAG auto-layouts and supports zoom, pan, and fit-to-screen controls

userStories.title: Environment Variable Management Per Workspace
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to manage environment variables per workspace so pipeline runs have the correct configuration without manual setup.
acceptanceCriteria: Migration creates a workspace_env_vars table with workspace_id, key, encrypted_value, is_secret, and updated_at columns
POST /api/workspaces/:id/env-vars creates or updates an env var; secret values are encrypted with AES-256-GCM
GET /api/workspaces/:id/env-vars returns all env vars with secret values masked as '••••••'
The pipeline trigger passes workspace env vars to the run-loop.sh process via environment injection
DELETE /api/workspaces/:id/env-vars/:key removes an env var and returns 204

userStories.title: Pipeline Pause and Resume
userStories.description: As a pipeline operator, I want to pause a running pipeline and resume it later so I can intervene when issues arise without losing progress.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/pipeline/runs/:id/pause sends SIGSTOP to the run-loop.sh process and updates status to 'paused'
POST /api/pipeline/runs/:id/resume sends SIGCONT and updates status back to 'running'
Pausing between stories is clean — the current story finishes before the pause takes effect
The pipeline monitor shows a Pause/Resume toggle button that reflects current run state
Paused runs emit a wal_event with event_type='run_paused' including elapsed time and completed story count

userStories.title: Run Comparison Side-by-Side
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to compare two pipeline runs side-by-side so I can identify regressions and improvements between spec versions.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/pipeline/runs/compare?run1=ID&run2=ID returns a structured comparison with per-story status differences
The comparison highlights stories that changed status (passed→failed, failed→passed, new, removed)
A CompareRunsPanel component renders both runs in parallel columns with matching stories aligned
Total pass rate, execution time, and token usage deltas are shown in a summary header
The comparison supports runs from different specs if story IDs overlap

userStories.title: Story Context Window Budget Tracking
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to see how much of the context window each story consumes so I can optimize prompts and avoid hitting token limits.
acceptanceCriteria: The pipeline engine records actual input_tokens and output_tokens from the Claude response for each story in story_results
GET /api/pipeline/runs/:id returns story_results with token usage fields included
A context budget bar shows consumed vs. available tokens (200k context window) for each story in the pipeline monitor
Stories exceeding 80% of the context window are flagged with a warning indicator
A summary chart shows total token consumption across all stories in the run

userStories.title: GitHub App Connection and Webhook Setup
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to connect my GitHub repository to a Rorcha workspace with one-click webhook installation so PR and commit events flow into Rorcha automatically.
acceptanceCriteria: A GitHubSettingsPanel component in workspace settings shows connection status and a 'Connect GitHub' button
POST /api/workspaces/:id/github/connect stores the repo owner, repo name, and webhook secret for the workspace
The endpoint creates a GitHub webhook via the GitHub API targeting POST /api/webhooks/github with push, pull_request, and issue events
GET /api/workspaces/:id/github returns connection status, repo info, and last webhook received timestamp
POST /api/workspaces/:id/github/disconnect removes the webhook from GitHub and clears the connection

userStories.title: GitHub Webhook Receiver with HMAC Verification
userStories.description: As a platform operator, I want incoming GitHub webhooks verified with HMAC-SHA256 so only authentic GitHub events are processed.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/webhooks/github verifies the X-Hub-Signature-256 header against the stored webhook secret using HMAC-SHA256
Invalid signatures return 401 with no processing — the raw body is used for signature computation (not parsed JSON)
Valid webhooks are dispatched to event-specific handlers based on the X-GitHub-Event header value
All received webhooks are logged in wal_events with event_type='github_webhook' and the event payload
The endpoint returns 200 immediately and processes events asynchronously to avoid GitHub timeout

userStories.title: PR-to-Spec Auto Sync
userStories.description: As a developer, I want merging a PR to automatically mark the corresponding story as passed in Rorcha so my spec status stays in sync with actual code delivery.
acceptanceCriteria: When a pull_request event with action 'closed' and merged=true is received, the handler extracts story IDs from the PR title and branch name
Story IDs are matched using the pattern feat(US-XXX) or feat/US-XXX-slug in the branch name or PR title
Matched stories are updated to passes=true in the spec JSON on disk and in story_results
A wal_event with event_type='github_pr_merged' is emitted with the PR URL, story IDs, and merge SHA
The spec detail UI shows a GitHub PR link icon on stories that were marked passed via PR merge

userStories.title: Commit-to-Story Mapping
userStories.description: As a developer, I want commits with feat(US-XXX) in their message automatically linked to the corresponding story so I can trace implementation back to requirements.
acceptanceCriteria: The push webhook handler parses commit messages for feat(STORY-ID) patterns and stores mappings in a story_commits table
Migration creates story_commits table with story_id, spec_id, commit_sha, commit_message, author, and pushed_at columns
GET /api/specs/:specId/stories/:storyId/commits returns all linked commits for a story
The story detail popover shows a 'Commits' section listing linked commits with SHA, message, and author
Multiple story IDs in a single commit message create multiple mapping rows

userStories.title: Auto-Branch Creation from Story
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to create a feature branch for any story with one click so I can start implementation immediately with a correctly named branch.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/specs/:specId/stories/:storyId/branch creates a git branch named feat/STORY-ID-slug in the workspace repository
The branch is created from the current HEAD of the default branch (main/master auto-detected)
The response includes the branch name and a suggested git checkout command
The story card UI shows a 'Create Branch' button that calls this endpoint and displays the result
If the branch already exists, return 409 with the existing branch name

userStories.title: Auto-Generated PR Description from Story
userStories.description: As a developer, I want PRs created from story branches to auto-populate the description with story details so reviewers have full context.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/specs/:specId/stories/:storyId/pr-body generates a PR description template from the story's title, description, and acceptance criteria
The template includes a checklist of acceptance criteria, the story's dependency list, and a link back to the Rorcha spec
The generated body is returned as Markdown text ready for the GitHub PR creation API or CLI
A 'Copy PR Body' button on the story card copies the generated description to clipboard
The template format is configurable per workspace via a pr_template field in workspace settings

userStories.title: Spec Compliance Status Check on PR
userStories.description: As a team lead, I want GitHub PRs to show a Rorcha status check indicating whether the linked story's acceptance criteria are covered so reviewers can verify completeness.
acceptanceCriteria: When a PR is opened or updated, Rorcha posts a GitHub commit status check (pending/success/failure) to the PR's head SHA
The check passes if all acceptance criteria for the linked story have corresponding test coverage (detected via keyword matching in changed files)
The check details URL links back to the Rorcha story detail view
POST /api/github/checks/:sha allows manual update of the check status for edge cases
The check name is 'rorcha/spec-compliance' and appears in the PR checks section

userStories.title: GitHub Issues Import to Stories
userStories.description: As a project manager, I want to import GitHub Issues as Rorcha stories so I can manage external requirements alongside generated specs.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/specs/:specId/import/github-issues accepts a list of GitHub issue numbers and creates corresponding stories in the spec
Imported stories map issue title→story title, issue body→description, and issue labels→tags
Each imported story includes a githubIssueUrl field linking back to the original issue
The import handles GitHub API pagination for repos with many issues
A preview mode returns the proposed stories without creating them, allowing user review before import

userStories.title: GitHub Actions YAML Generator
userStories.description: As a DevOps engineer, I want to generate a GitHub Actions workflow YAML that triggers Rorcha pipeline runs so I can integrate spec execution into my CI/CD pipeline.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/workspaces/:id/github/actions-yaml generates a GitHub Actions workflow file targeting the Rorcha API
The workflow triggers on push to main branch and calls POST /api/pipeline/trigger with the workspace's latest approved spec
The YAML includes proper secrets references for RORCHA_API_TOKEN and WORKSPACE_ID
The generated file includes job steps for: checkout, trigger Rorcha pipeline, wait for completion via polling, report status
A 'Download Actions YAML' button in workspace settings triggers the download

userStories.title: Team Creation and Invite System
userStories.description: As a team owner, I want to create a team and invite members via email so we can collaborate on specs and pipeline management.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/teams creates a team with name and slug; the creating user becomes the owner (admin role)
POST /api/teams/:id/invites sends an email invitation with a signed invite token (valid 7 days)
GET /api/invites/:token validates the token and returns team info; POST /api/invites/:token/accept adds the user to the team
GET /api/teams/:id/members lists all members with their roles, join dates, and last active timestamps
Team owners can have at most 3 pending invites at a time on the free tier

userStories.title: Role-Based Access Control Middleware
userStories.description: As a platform operator, I want role-based permissions enforced on all team resources so viewers can't modify specs and only admins can manage team settings.
acceptanceCriteria: A requireRole('admin'|'editor'|'viewer') middleware checks the user's team role before allowing the request
Viewers can read specs, runs, and analytics but cannot create, edit, approve, or trigger pipelines
Editors can do everything viewers can plus create/edit specs, approve specs, and trigger pipelines
Admins can do everything editors can plus manage team members, workspace settings, and billing
Unauthorized actions return 403 with error 'Insufficient permissions: requires {role} role'

userStories.title: Spec Review Workflow with Request-Approval State
userStories.description: As a team member, I want a formal review workflow where specs go through a request-approval cycle so changes are peer-reviewed before execution.
acceptanceCriteria: Specs gain a reviewStatus field: draft → review_requested → approved → changes_requested
POST /api/specs/:id/request-review transitions status to review_requested and notifies team admins/editors
POST /api/specs/:id/review accepts action (approve/request_changes) and optional comment
The spec list shows review status badges and filters for 'Needs Review' and 'Changes Requested'
Review history is stored in wal_events with reviewer ID, action, and comment for audit trail

userStories.title: Inline Comments on Stories
userStories.description: As a team reviewer, I want to leave comments on individual stories within a spec so I can provide targeted feedback during the review process.
acceptanceCriteria: Migration creates a story_comments table with id, spec_id, story_id, user_id, body (Markdown), created_at, resolved_at columns
POST /api/specs/:specId/stories/:storyId/comments creates a comment; GET retrieves all comments for a story
Comments support Markdown formatting and display the author's name and avatar
POST /api/specs/:specId/stories/:storyId/comments/:commentId/resolve marks a comment as resolved
Unresolved comment count is shown as a badge on each story card in the spec detail view

userStories.title: Activity Feed
userStories.description: As a team member, I want an activity feed showing who approved, rejected, edited, and ran specs so I have visibility into team activity.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/activity returns a paginated feed of recent actions across all workspace specs and runs
Each activity item includes: actor (user), action type, target (spec/run/story), timestamp, and optional detail text
Activity types include: spec_created, spec_edited, spec_approved, spec_rejected, run_triggered, run_completed, comment_added, member_joined
An ActivityFeedPanel component renders the feed as a timeline with user avatars and action descriptions
Activity items link to the relevant spec, run, or story when clicked

userStories.title: Shared Direction Layer Library
userStories.description: As a team admin, I want shared direction layers (L1 and L2) that apply across all team workspaces so we maintain consistent engineering standards.
acceptanceCriteria: Direction layers L1 and L2 can be scoped to a team_id in addition to the existing workspace and domain scoping
Team-scoped L1/L2 layers override global defaults but are overridden by workspace-specific L3+ layers
PUT /api/teams/:id/direction creates or updates team-level direction layers
GET /api/direction for any team workspace includes the team's L1/L2 layers in the synthesis
A TeamDirectionPanel component allows admins to edit team direction layers with a preview of the merged output

userStories.title: Team Template Marketplace
userStories.description: As a team member, I want to browse and use spec templates shared by my team so I can leverage proven patterns without recreating them.
acceptanceCriteria: Templates gain an optional team_id field; team templates are visible to all team members
GET /api/templates accepts a scope parameter: 'personal', 'team', or 'all' to filter template visibility
A TemplateMarketplacePanel shows team templates as cards with usage count, author, and rating
POST /api/templates/:id/rate allows team members to rate templates on a 1-5 scale
Templates with average rating >= 4.0 are featured at the top of the marketplace

userStories.title: Spec Assignment to Team Members
userStories.description: As a team lead, I want to assign specs and individual stories to team members so ownership and responsibility are clear.
acceptanceCriteria: Specs and stories gain an optional assignee_id field referencing a user in the team
PUT /api/specs/:id with assigneeId assigns the entire spec; PUT /api/specs/:specId/stories/:storyId with assigneeId assigns a story
GET /api/specs accepts an assignee parameter to filter specs by assigned user
The spec detail view shows assignee avatars on spec headers and story cards with a dropdown to reassign
GET /api/users/me/assigned returns all specs and stories assigned to the current user across workspaces

userStories.title: Real-Time Token Usage Dashboard
userStories.description: As a cost-conscious team lead, I want a real-time dashboard showing token usage per spec, story, model, and user so I can monitor and control spending.
acceptanceCriteria: Migration creates a token_usage table with run_id, story_id, user_id, model, input_tokens, output_tokens, cost_usd, and recorded_at columns
The pipeline engine records token usage from Claude responses into this table after each story completes
GET /api/analytics/usage accepts date range, group_by (spec/story/model/user), and returns aggregated usage data
A UsageDashboardPanel renders bar charts (by model), line charts (over time), and summary cards (total tokens, total cost)
The dashboard auto-refreshes every 30 seconds during active pipeline runs

userStories.title: Cost Breakdown with Provider Pricing
userStories.description: As a billing admin, I want cost breakdowns calculated using actual provider pricing so I can see real dollar amounts per spec and run.
acceptanceCriteria: Migration creates a model_pricing table with model_id, provider, input_cost_per_1m_tokens, output_cost_per_1m_tokens, and effective_date columns
Default pricing rows are seeded for claude-sonnet-4-5, claude-haiku-4-5, and claude-opus-4 on migration
GET /api/analytics/costs returns cost breakdowns grouped by spec, run, model, and time period
Cost calculation: (input_tokens * input_rate + output_tokens * output_rate) per story, summed per grouping
An admin UI allows updating pricing when providers change rates

userStories.title: Budget Alerts and Hard Caps
userStories.description: As a team admin, I want to set budget alerts and hard spending caps so unexpected costs are caught and controlled.
acceptanceCriteria: Migration creates a budget_config table with workspace_id, alert_threshold_usd, hard_cap_usd, period (daily/weekly/monthly), and notify_emails columns
POST /api/workspaces/:id/budget creates or updates budget configuration
When spending exceeds alert_threshold, a wal_event with event_type='budget_alert' is emitted and email notification queued
When spending exceeds hard_cap, new pipeline triggers are blocked with 409 error 'Budget cap exceeded for this period'
GET /api/workspaces/:id/budget returns current config, spending so far this period, and remaining budget

userStories.title: BYOB API Key Vault
userStories.description: As a pro user, I want to store my own API keys securely so I can use premium models with my own billing account.
acceptanceCriteria: Migration creates an api_key_vault table with user_id, provider, encrypted_key, label, spend_total_usd, and created_at columns
POST /api/vault/keys stores an API key encrypted with AES-256-GCM; the plaintext is never returned after creation
GET /api/vault/keys lists stored keys with provider, label, last_used_at, and spend_total masked key (last 4 chars only)
When generating specs or running pipelines, the user's vault key is used if available for the selected model's provider
DELETE /api/vault/keys/:id removes a key; spend tracking is retained for historical records

userStories.title: Model Comparison Matrix
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a comparison view showing cost, quality, and speed metrics across models so I can choose the best model for each use case.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/analytics/models returns aggregated metrics per model: avg cost per story, avg time per story, pass rate, and total usage
A ModelComparisonPanel renders a table/matrix with models as rows and metrics as columns, sortable by any column
Metrics are calculated from historical story_results and token_usage data across all runs
Each model row includes a 'Use this model' button that sets it as the workspace preferred_model
Models with fewer than 5 story completions show an 'Insufficient data' label instead of metrics

userStories.title: Sprint Velocity Chart
userStories.description: As a project manager, I want a velocity chart showing stories completed per week so I can track team productivity over time.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/analytics/velocity accepts a date range and returns weekly story completion counts grouped by status (passed/failed/skipped)
A VelocityChartPanel renders a stacked bar chart with weeks on the x-axis and story counts on the y-axis
The chart includes a trend line showing the rolling 4-week average velocity
Hovering over a bar shows a tooltip with the exact counts and notable specs completed that week
The panel includes a filter dropdown to scope velocity to a specific workspace or spec

userStories.title: Completion Rate Analytics by Story Type
userStories.description: As a team lead, I want to see completion rates broken down by story complexity and type so I can identify where the AI struggles and optimize accordingly.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/analytics/completion-rates returns pass/fail/skip percentages grouped by complexity score (1-5)
The response includes breakdown by story tag if tags are present, showing which categories have lowest pass rates
A CompletionRatePanel renders horizontal bar charts with pass rate percentages per group
Groups with pass rate below 60% are highlighted in red as improvement opportunities
The data covers a configurable time range with 30-day default

userStories.title: CSV/JSON Analytics Export
userStories.description: As an analyst, I want to export usage and analytics data as CSV or JSON so I can perform custom analysis in external tools.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/analytics/export accepts format (csv/json), data_type (usage/costs/velocity/completion), and date range parameters
CSV exports include proper headers and RFC 4180 compliant formatting with quoted fields containing commas
JSON exports follow the same structure as the corresponding analytics API responses
The response sets Content-Disposition header for file download with timestamp in filename
Export is limited to 10,000 rows per request with a Link header pointing to the next page if truncated

userStories.title: Command Palette with Fuzzy Search
userStories.description: As a power user, I want a Cmd+K command palette with fuzzy search so I can quickly navigate to any spec, story, run, or action without clicking through menus.
acceptanceCriteria: Pressing Cmd+K (or Ctrl+K) opens a modal command palette with a search input at the top
The palette searches across: specs (by title), stories (by ID/title), runs (by ID/spec), and actions (approve, trigger, settings)
Results use fuzzy matching (e.g., 'auth reg' matches 'User Authentication Registration') and are ranked by relevance
Selecting a result navigates to the relevant page/panel or executes the action immediately
Recent commands are shown when the palette opens with no query, keyboard arrows navigate results, and Enter selects

userStories.title: Keyboard Shortcut Reference Panel
userStories.description: As a power user, I want a keyboard shortcut reference panel so I can learn and use shortcuts to navigate Rorcha faster.
acceptanceCriteria: Pressing ? or Cmd+/ opens a shortcuts reference panel showing all available keyboard shortcuts
Shortcuts are grouped by category: Navigation, Spec Actions, Pipeline Actions, and Global
Core shortcuts include: Cmd+K (palette), Cmd+Enter (approve), Cmd+Shift+R (trigger run), Esc (close panels)
The panel is dismissible by pressing Esc or clicking outside it
Shortcuts are registered globally using a useHotkeys hook that handles platform-specific modifier keys (Cmd vs Ctrl)

userStories.title: Dark/Light/System Theme Toggle
userStories.description: As a user, I want to switch between dark, light, and system-matched themes so I can work comfortably in any lighting condition.
acceptanceCriteria: A ThemeProvider context wraps the app with 'light', 'dark', and 'system' modes stored in localStorage
Tailwind dark mode classes are applied conditionally based on the active theme
The theme toggle appears in the top navigation bar as a three-state icon button (sun/moon/monitor)
System mode uses prefers-color-scheme media query and updates reactively when OS setting changes
All existing UI components maintain WCAG AA contrast ratios in both light and dark themes

userStories.title: Mobile Responsive Layout Overhaul
userStories.description: As a mobile user, I want the Rorcha interface to be fully usable on phones and tablets so I can check spec status and approve on the go.
acceptanceCriteria: All panels render correctly on viewports from 320px to 1440px using Tailwind responsive breakpoints
The sidebar collapses to a hamburger menu on screens below 768px with a slide-out drawer
Touch targets are minimum 44px on mobile; tap-to-edit replaces hover interactions
The pipeline monitor terminal uses a mobile-optimized font size and supports horizontal scroll for wide output
A meta viewport tag ensures proper scaling on mobile Safari and Chrome

userStories.title: Onboarding Wizard for First Workspace
userStories.description: As a new user, I want a guided onboarding wizard so I can set up my first workspace quickly without reading documentation.
acceptanceCriteria: First-time login (no workspaces) shows a multi-step wizard: Welcome → Connect Repository → Configure Direction Stack → Generate First Spec
Step 1 collects the workspace path via file browser or manual entry and validates it's a git repository
Step 2 presents L1-L3 direction layer templates with sensible defaults for common stacks (React, Node, Python, etc.)
Step 3 offers a sample brief and triggers a real spec generation so the user sees the full flow
Progress is persisted so users can close the browser and resume the wizard where they left off

userStories.title: Contextual Help Tooltips
userStories.description: As a new user, I want contextual help tooltips on complex UI elements so I can understand features without leaving the page.
acceptanceCriteria: A HelpTooltip component wraps complex UI elements and shows a (?) icon that reveals help text on hover/click
Tooltips are defined in a centralized help-content.ts file with keys matching component names
Tooltips appear for: Direction Stack layers, complexity scores, readiness percentage, pipeline parallelism, and cost estimates
A 'Show tips' toggle in user settings enables/disables all contextual tooltips globally
Tooltips support Markdown formatting and optional 'Learn more' links to documentation

userStories.title: OpenAPI/Swagger Documentation Portal
userStories.description: As an API consumer, I want auto-generated OpenAPI documentation so I can explore and test Rorcha's REST API without reading source code.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/docs serves a Swagger UI page generated from an OpenAPI 3.0 spec file
The OpenAPI spec covers all API routes with request/response schemas, status codes, and example payloads
Authentication is documented with Bearer token scheme and the UI supports 'Authorize' to test authenticated endpoints
The spec file is generated from JSDoc annotations on route handlers using swagger-jsdoc
GET /api/docs/openapi.json returns the raw OpenAPI spec for programmatic consumption

userStories.title: Import from Linear/GitHub Issues
userStories.description: As a project manager, I want to import issues from Linear and GitHub Issues as Rorcha stories so I can consolidate project management in one tool.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/specs/:id/import accepts a source parameter ('linear' or 'github') and source-specific credentials/filters
Linear import uses the Linear API to fetch issues by project/team and maps title→story title, description→description, labels→tags
GitHub import fetches issues by repo and milestone with the same field mapping
A preview step shows the proposed stories before committing the import to the spec
Imported stories include a sourceUrl field linking back to the original issue in Linear or GitHub

userStories.title: Rorcha CLI: Core Commands
userStories.description: As a CLI power user, I want a rorcha CLI tool with generate, run, status, and approve commands so I can manage specs without opening a browser.
acceptanceCriteria: An npm package @rorcha/cli provides the rorcha command with subcommands: generate, run, status, approve, and login
rorcha login authenticates via browser OAuth redirect and stores the JWT in ~/.rorcha/credentials
rorcha generate --brief 'description' calls POST /api/specs/generate and prints the generated spec summary
rorcha run <spec-id> calls POST /api/pipeline/trigger and streams terminal output to stdout
rorcha status shows the current pipeline run status with story progress indicators

userStories.title: VS Code Extension: Spec Viewer and Actions
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a VS Code extension that shows my Rorcha specs and lets me approve and trigger runs so I can work without context-switching to a browser.
acceptanceCriteria: A VS Code extension 'rorcha-vscode' adds a sidebar panel listing specs from the connected Rorcha instance
Each spec in the tree view shows status, story count, and readiness percentage
Right-click actions on specs include: Approve, Trigger Run, Open in Browser, and Copy Spec JSON
The extension reads the Rorcha server URL from VS Code settings or auto-detects from workspace CLAUDE.md
Extension authenticates using the same JWT stored by the CLI at ~/.rorcha/credentials

userStories.title: PostgreSQL Migration Path
userStories.description: As a platform operator scaling beyond a single server, I want a PostgreSQL migration path so I can use a production-grade database while keeping SQLite as the zero-config default.
acceptanceCriteria: A DATABASE_URL environment variable switches the backend from SQLite to PostgreSQL when set to a postgres:// connection string
A database abstraction layer wraps both better-sqlite3 and pg with the same query interface (prepare/get/all/run)
All existing SQL queries are compatible with both SQLite and PostgreSQL dialects (no SQLite-specific functions without fallbacks)
Migration files are versioned and run on both databases using a dialect-aware runner
A data export script dumps SQLite data as SQL INSERT statements importable by PostgreSQL

userStories.title: Docker Compose Deployment
userStories.description: As a DevOps engineer, I want a Docker Compose setup for Rorcha so I can deploy the full stack with a single command.
acceptanceCriteria: A docker-compose.yml defines services: rorcha-frontend (nginx serving built assets), rorcha-backend (Node.js), and optionally rorcha-db (PostgreSQL)
Multi-stage Dockerfiles build production images under 200MB for both frontend and backend
Environment variables are configurable via .env file with documented defaults in .env.example
Volumes are mounted for database persistence (/data/rorcha.db for SQLite or PostgreSQL data directory)
docker compose up starts all services with health checks and automatic restart on failure

userStories.title: Automated Database Backup
userStories.description: As a platform operator, I want automated database backups so I can recover from data loss or corruption.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/admin/backup triggers an immediate backup; a cron job runs daily backups automatically
SQLite backups use the .backup() API for a consistent snapshot while the WAL is active
PostgreSQL backups use pg_dump piped to gzip for compressed output
Backups are stored locally in a configurable BACKUP_DIR with timestamped filenames and 30-day retention
GET /api/admin/backups lists available backups with filename, size, and creation timestamp

userStories.title: Health Monitoring and Uptime Checks
userStories.description: As a platform operator, I want health monitoring endpoints so I can integrate with uptime services and detect issues proactively.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/health returns 200 with {status, version, uptime, db_connected, active_runs} — already partially exists, extend it
GET /api/health/detailed returns additional metrics: db_size, pending_specs_count, memory_usage, and last_backup_at
The health endpoint checks database connectivity by executing a simple query and reports failure if it times out (>1s)
Health check responses include cache headers preventing CDN/proxy caching
A HealthDashboard admin panel visualizes uptime history using data from periodic health check results stored in wal_events

userStories.title: Rate Limiting Per User and IP
userStories.description: As a platform operator, I want rate limiting on API endpoints so the system is protected from abuse and overload.
acceptanceCriteria: A rate limiter middleware tracks requests per user (authenticated) or per IP (unauthenticated) using an in-memory sliding window
Default limits: 100 requests/minute for authenticated users, 20 requests/minute for unauthenticated
LLM-calling endpoints (spec generation, pipeline trigger) have a stricter limit of 10 requests/minute
Rate-limited responses return 429 with Retry-After header indicating seconds until the window resets
Rate limit configuration is stored in a rate_limits table allowing per-endpoint and per-tier customization

userStories.title: Audit Log UI with Filter and Search
userStories.description: As a team admin, I want a searchable audit log UI so I can investigate who did what and when across the platform.
acceptanceCriteria: An AuditLogPanel component renders wal_events as a filterable, searchable table with timestamp, actor, event type, and details columns
Filters include: event type dropdown, date range picker, actor search, and workspace selector
Full-text search across event payloads finds specific spec names, story IDs, or error messages
Results are paginated with 50 items per page and support both newest-first and oldest-first sort
Clicking an audit row expands to show the full event payload as formatted JSON

userStories.title: Expanded MCP Tool Set: Spec Management
userStories.description: As a Claude Code user, I want additional MCP tools for spec editing, story management, and search so I can manage the full spec lifecycle from my editor.
acceptanceCriteria: MCP tool rorcha_edit_story allows updating a single story's title, description, and acceptance criteria by spec ID and story ID
MCP tool rorcha_search_stories performs cross-spec story search with query string and returns matching stories with context
MCP tool rorcha_add_stories appends new stories to an existing spec
MCP tool rorcha_delete_story removes a story from a spec by ID
All new MCP tools include proper JSON schema validation and helpful error messages for invalid parameters

userStories.title: Expanded MCP Tool Set: Pipeline and Analytics
userStories.description: As a Claude Code user, I want MCP tools for pipeline control and analytics so I can monitor and manage runs from within my AI-assisted workflow.
acceptanceCriteria: MCP tool rorcha_trigger_run starts a pipeline run for a given spec ID with optional parallelism and dry-run parameters
MCP tool rorcha_run_status returns the current run status with per-story progress for a given run ID
MCP tool rorcha_usage_stats returns token usage and cost summary for a date range
MCP tool rorcha_retry_story retries a single failed story within a completed run
MCP tool rorcha_list_runs returns recent pipeline runs with status, spec, and completion summary

userStories.title: Agent Hooks System
userStories.description: As a power user, I want to register shell commands as hooks that fire on Rorcha events so I can integrate custom automation into the spec lifecycle.
acceptanceCriteria: Migration creates an agent_hooks table with workspace_id, event_type, command, enabled, timeout_seconds, and created_at columns
Supported event types: on_generate, on_approve, on_reject, on_run_start, on_run_complete, on_story_pass, on_story_fail
POST /api/workspaces/:id/hooks creates a hook; PUT updates; DELETE removes
When an event fires, matching hooks execute asynchronously with event data passed as JSON in the RORCHA_EVENT environment variable
Hook execution results (exit code, stdout, stderr) are logged in wal_events with event_type='hook_executed'

userStories.title: Custom Agent Profiles Per Workspace
userStories.description: As a platform admin, I want custom agent profiles that override system prompts and tool restrictions per workspace so I can tailor AI behavior to different projects.
acceptanceCriteria: Migration creates an agent_profiles table with workspace_id, name, system_prompt_override, allowed_tools JSON array, and model_override columns
POST /api/workspaces/:id/agent-profiles creates a profile; GET lists profiles for a workspace
When pipeline runs trigger Claude, the active agent profile's system prompt is prepended to the direction stack
Allowed_tools restricts which MCP tools the agent can use during execution (empty array = all tools allowed)
A default profile is auto-created for each workspace using the workspace's direction stack L3 content

userStories.title: MCP Tool: Direction Stack Management
userStories.description: As a Claude Code user, I want MCP tools to read and update direction stack layers so I can configure project context without leaving my editor.
acceptanceCriteria: MCP tool rorcha_get_direction returns the full direction stack for a workspace with all layers and their content
MCP tool rorcha_update_direction updates a specific layer (L1-L5) for a workspace or domain
MCP tool rorcha_synthesize_direction returns the merged/synthesized direction string as it would be sent to the LLM
All direction tools accept workspace_id as a required parameter for workspace-scoped operations
Changes made via MCP tools are reflected immediately in subsequent spec generations

userStories.title: MCP Tool: Workspace and Team Management
userStories.description: As a Claude Code user, I want MCP tools to manage workspaces and view team info so I can perform administrative tasks from within my coding session.
acceptanceCriteria: MCP tool rorcha_list_workspaces returns all workspaces the user has access to with path, label, and domain
MCP tool rorcha_create_workspace registers a new workspace by path with label and domain parameters
MCP tool rorcha_workspace_stats returns summary stats: spec count, run count, pass rate, and last activity
MCP tool rorcha_team_members returns the team member list for a given workspace if team-scoped
All workspace tools validate the user's permissions before returning data

userStories.title: Notification System: Email and In-App
userStories.description: As a team member, I want notifications for important events so I stay informed about spec reviews, pipeline completions, and mentions without constantly checking the dashboard.
acceptanceCriteria: Migration creates a notifications table with user_id, type, title, body, read_at, created_at, and link columns
In-app notifications appear as a bell icon badge in the top nav with unread count
Clicking the bell opens a dropdown showing recent notifications; clicking one navigates to the linked resource
Email notifications are sent for: review requests, spec approvals/rejections, pipeline completions, budget alerts, and @mentions
Users can configure notification preferences per event type (in-app only, email only, both, none) via settings

userStories.title: @Mention Notifications in Comments
userStories.description: As a team collaborator, I want to @mention teammates in story comments so they receive a notification and can quickly respond.
acceptanceCriteria: Comment bodies support @username syntax that is parsed and linked to user accounts
An autocomplete dropdown appears when typing @ in a comment, showing team members filtered by input
@mentioned users receive an in-app notification with link to the specific story comment
Mentioned usernames are rendered as clickable links showing the user's profile on hover
Multiple mentions in a single comment each generate separate notifications

userStories.title: Spec Version History with Visual Diff
userStories.description: As a spec author, I want a visual diff view comparing any two spec versions so I can review what changed between edits or regenerations.
acceptanceCriteria: The spec detail view includes a 'History' tab showing all versions with timestamps, author, and change summary
Selecting two versions opens a side-by-side diff view with added stories in green, removed in red, and modified in yellow
Modified stories show per-field diffs highlighting the specific text changes in title, description, and acceptance criteria
A 'Restore this version' button on any historical version creates a new version with the restored content
The diff view reuses the existing GET /api/specs/:id/diff endpoint with enhanced frontend rendering

userStories.title: Smart Dependency Detection
userStories.description: As a spec author, I want the AI to automatically detect and suggest story dependencies based on content analysis so I don't have to manually wire every relationship.
acceptanceCriteria: During spec generation, the LLM prompt includes instructions to analyze stories and populate dependsOn fields
POST /api/specs/:id/detect-dependencies runs a separate LLM call to analyze existing stories and suggest missing dependencies
Suggested dependencies are returned as proposals that the user can accept or reject individually
The UI shows suggested dependencies as dashed arrows in the dependency DAG with accept/reject controls
Circular dependencies are detected and rejected with an error identifying the cycle

userStories.title: AI-Generated Acceptance Criteria Enhancement
userStories.description: As a spec author, I want to auto-enhance sparse acceptance criteria with AI-generated suggestions so every story meets the minimum quality bar.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/specs/:specId/stories/:storyId/enhance-criteria calls the LLM with the story context and generates additional acceptance criteria
Enhanced criteria are returned as suggestions appended below existing criteria with visual distinction
Users can accept individual suggestions, accept all, or dismiss all with one click
The enhancement prompt considers the direction stack context and related stories for consistency
Stories with fewer than 3 criteria show a 'Suggest more criteria' prompt in the UI

userStories.title: Pipeline Retry with Story Selection
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to retry failed stories from a completed run without re-running successful ones so I can fix issues incrementally.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/pipeline/runs/:id/retry accepts an optional storyIds array; defaults to all failed stories if omitted
Retried stories create a new pipeline_run linked to the original run via a retried_from_run_id field
Successful stories from the original run are not re-executed; their results are copied to the new run
The pipeline monitor shows retry runs with a badge indicating they're partial retries
Retry runs use the same spec version and direction stack as the original run for consistency

userStories.title: Worktree Merge UI with Conflict Detection
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the worktree merge UI to detect and display merge conflicts so I can resolve them before completing the merge.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/worktrees/merge/preview performs a dry-run merge and returns conflict status without modifying any branches
If conflicts exist, the response includes a list of conflicting files with conflict markers extracted
The WorktreeMergePanel shows conflicting files with a visual diff and per-file resolve/skip toggles
A force merge option is available for admins that accepts the target branch version for all conflicts
Successful merges create a wal_event with event_type='worktree_merged' including the branch name and merge commit SHA

userStories.title: Pipeline Output Log Persistence
userStories.description: As a developer, I want pipeline output logs persisted to disk so I can review terminal output from past runs even after backend restarts.
acceptanceCriteria: Pipeline terminal output is written to a log file at workspace.path/scripts/ralph/logs/run-{runId}.log as it streams
The in-memory buffer is still used for live streaming but the disk log serves as the persistent fallback
GET /api/pipeline/runs/:id/output falls back to reading from the disk log file when the in-memory buffer is empty
Log files are retained for 30 days; a cleanup job deletes older logs on backend startup
The run detail view shows a 'Download Log' button that serves the raw log file

userStories.title: Spec Generation Model Selection UI
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to choose which AI model generates my spec so I can balance cost and quality per generation.
acceptanceCriteria: The spec generation form includes a model selector dropdown populated from GET /api/direction/models
The selected model is passed to POST /api/specs/generate and used for that generation only
The dropdown shows model name, provider, estimated cost per 1K tokens, and a 'recommended' badge on the workspace default
Model selection persists in the form for the session but doesn't change the workspace default
If the selected model fails (API error), the error message includes the model name and a suggestion to try an alternative

userStories.title: Batch Spec Generation
userStories.description: As a project lead, I want to generate multiple specs from a list of briefs in one operation so I can bootstrap an entire project backlog quickly.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/specs/generate/batch accepts an array of brief objects each with title and brief fields
Briefs are processed sequentially to avoid LLM rate limits; progress is streamed via SSE
Each generated spec is saved individually with its own slug and version history
The batch endpoint returns a summary with success/failure counts and per-spec result details
Failed generations include the error message and do not block remaining briefs in the batch

userStories.title: Story Exclusion Toggle with Pipeline Integration
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to exclude specific stories from pipeline runs without deleting them so I can skip problematic or out-of-scope stories temporarily.
acceptanceCriteria: Each story supports an excluded boolean field (default false) in the spec JSON
PUT /api/specs/:specId/stories/:storyId with excluded=true marks the story as excluded
The pipeline engine skips excluded stories and marks them as 'excluded' in story_results
Excluded stories appear grayed out in the spec detail view with a toggle to re-include
Bulk exclude/include is supported via the bulk operations endpoint

userStories.title: ROI Calculator
userStories.description: As a decision maker, I want an ROI calculator estimating developer hours saved by Rorcha so I can justify the platform investment to stakeholders.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/analytics/roi calculates estimated hours saved based on: stories passed * configurable hours_per_story (default 4h) minus LLM cost converted at hourly_rate
The ROI response includes: total_stories_passed, estimated_hours_saved, total_llm_cost, net_savings, and roi_multiplier
An ROIPanel component displays the metrics as large summary numbers with a trend chart over time
The hours_per_story and hourly_rate parameters are configurable per workspace in settings
The calculation accounts for retried stories to avoid double-counting savings

userStories.title: User Settings and Preferences Panel
userStories.description: As a user, I want a settings panel where I can manage my profile, API keys, notification preferences, and display options.
acceptanceCriteria: A SettingsPanel component is accessible from the user avatar menu in the top navigation
Profile section allows updating display name, avatar URL, and password (for email auth users)
Notifications section shows per-event-type toggles for in-app and email delivery
API Keys section lists stored BYOB keys with add/remove functionality (shows last 4 chars only)
Display section includes theme toggle, default model preference, and items-per-page setting

userStories.title: Workspace Settings Panel
userStories.description: As a workspace admin, I want a workspace settings panel to manage direction stack, GitHub connection, environment variables, and pipeline configuration in one place.
acceptanceCriteria: A WorkspaceSettingsPanel component is accessible from the workspace dropdown with tabs: General, Direction Stack, GitHub, Env Vars, Pipeline, Hooks
General tab shows workspace label, path, domain, and default model with edit controls
Each tab section maps to existing API endpoints and provides CRUD UI for that configuration area
Changes are saved per-section with a 'Save' button and success/error toast notifications
The panel validates workspace path exists on the filesystem before saving

userStories.title: Error Boundary and Global Error Handling
userStories.description: As a user, I want graceful error handling throughout the UI so crashes show helpful messages instead of blank screens.
acceptanceCriteria: A React ErrorBoundary wraps all panel components and catches render errors with a fallback UI showing the error and a retry button
API errors from apiFetch are intercepted by a global error handler that shows toast notifications with the error message
Network failures show a 'Connection lost — retrying...' banner that auto-dismisses when connectivity resumes
401 errors trigger automatic redirect to the login page with a return URL for post-login redirect
Unhandled promise rejections are caught by a global handler and logged to the console with a user-facing toast

userStories.title: Sidebar Navigation Overhaul
userStories.description: As a user, I want a redesigned sidebar with grouped navigation, quick actions, and workspace switcher so I can navigate the expanded platform efficiently.
acceptanceCriteria: The sidebar groups nav items into collapsible sections: Specs (Forge, Review, Archive), Pipeline (Monitor, Schedules, Runs), Analytics, and Settings
A workspace switcher dropdown at the top of the sidebar shows the current workspace with quick-switch capability
Quick action buttons at the bottom provide one-click access to: New Spec, Trigger Run, and Command Palette
Active panel is highlighted with a colored left border; section badges show counts (pending specs, active runs)
The sidebar can be collapsed to icon-only mode with a toggle button, persisting the preference in localStorage

userStories.title: Spec Forge Panel Redesign
userStories.description: As a user, I want the spec generation form redesigned with better UX including template selection, model picker, context extraction, and generation progress so the spec creation flow feels premium.
acceptanceCriteria: The Spec Forge panel layout is reorganized into a step flow: Select Template → Write Brief → Configure → Generate
The brief input expands to a rich text editor with Markdown preview and drag-drop file attachment for context
A progress indicator shows generation stages: Analyzing Brief → Building Direction Stack → Generating Stories → Validating Output
Generation errors show inline with suggested fixes (e.g., 'Brief too vague — add more specific requirements')
The panel remembers the last used template and model selection for convenience

userStories.title: Spec Detail Panel Redesign
userStories.description: As a user, I want the spec detail view redesigned with tabs for stories, diagram, history, comments, and settings so all spec information is organized and accessible.
acceptanceCriteria: The spec detail view uses a tabbed layout: Stories (default), Diagram, History, Comments, and Settings
The Stories tab shows story cards with inline edit, complexity badge, assignment avatar, and status indicators
A story filter bar supports filtering by status (all/passed/failed/pending/excluded), complexity, and assignee
The header shows spec title, readiness percentage, tag chips, review status, and action buttons (Approve, Run, Fork)
Story cards support expand/collapse for acceptance criteria and comments without navigating away

userStories.title: Pipeline Monitor Panel Redesign
userStories.description: As a user, I want the pipeline monitor redesigned with a split view showing the dependency DAG alongside the terminal output so I can track progress visually and technically.
acceptanceCriteria: The pipeline monitor uses a horizontal split layout: DAG view on the left (40%) and terminal on the right (60%)
The split is resizable via drag handle and the layout preference persists
A story list sidebar can replace the DAG view for users who prefer a simpler interface (toggle button)
The header shows run status, elapsed time, stories completed/total progress bar, and pause/cancel buttons
Clicking a node in the DAG switches the terminal to that story's output (filtered from the full log)

userStories.title: Dashboard Home Panel
userStories.description: As a user, I want a dashboard home panel showing key metrics, recent activity, and quick actions so I have a useful landing page after login.
acceptanceCriteria: A DashboardPanel component renders as the default landing page after login with workspace context
Summary cards show: total specs, pending reviews, active runs, this week's pass rate, and estimated cost savings
A 'Recent Activity' section shows the last 10 actions across all workspaces with links
Quick action buttons for 'New Spec', 'Trigger Run', and 'Open Archive' are prominently placed
The dashboard auto-refreshes every 30 seconds to reflect real-time pipeline status changes

userStories.title: API Pagination Standardization
userStories.description: As an API consumer, I want all list endpoints to use a consistent pagination format so client code is predictable and reusable.
acceptanceCriteria: All list endpoints return { items: T[], total: number, hasMore: boolean, cursor?: string } format
Query parameters page (1-indexed), limit (default 50, max 250), and cursor are supported uniformly
Cursor-based pagination uses an opaque encoded string (base64 of last item's sort key) for stable iteration
The cursor parameter takes precedence over page when both are provided
A shared paginateQuery utility function in the backend handles pagination logic for all routes

userStories.title: Backend Error Standardization
userStories.description: As an API consumer, I want all error responses to follow a consistent format so client error handling is uniform.
acceptanceCriteria: All error responses return { error: string, code?: string, details?: object } with appropriate HTTP status codes
A centralized error handler middleware catches unhandled errors and formats them consistently
Known error types (ValidationError, NotFoundError, ConflictError, AuthError) are defined as typed classes
Stack traces are never included in production responses (only in development when NODE_ENV=development)
Validation errors include a details object with per-field error messages

userStories.title: Frontend State Management with Context
userStories.description: As a frontend developer, I want a structured state management pattern using React Context so global state (auth, workspace, theme, notifications) is manageable and testable.
acceptanceCriteria: AuthContext manages user authentication state, token refresh, and login/logout actions
WorkspaceContext (existing) is extended with team info, settings, and active run state
NotificationContext manages the notification bell state with unread count and real-time updates via SSE
ThemeContext manages dark/light/system mode preference with localStorage persistence
Each context provider includes a corresponding useAuth, useWorkspace, useNotifications, useTheme hook for consumption

userStories.title: Frontend API Client Refactor
userStories.description: As a frontend developer, I want a typed API client layer that wraps apiFetch with endpoint-specific functions so API calls are type-safe and consistent.
acceptanceCriteria: An api/ directory contains typed functions for each API resource: specs.ts, pipeline.ts, auth.ts, analytics.ts, teams.ts
Each function returns typed responses matching the backend API contracts (e.g., listSpecs(): Promise<SpecListResponse>)
The base apiFetch is extended with automatic token refresh on 401 responses before retrying the original request
Error responses are parsed and thrown as typed ApiError objects with status, code, and message fields
All API functions accept AbortSignal for cancellation support in React effects

userStories.title: End-to-End Test Suite for Critical Paths
userStories.description: As a developer, I want E2E tests covering the critical user journeys so regressions in the full-stack flow are caught before deployment.
acceptanceCriteria: Playwright test suite covers: login flow, spec generation, spec approval, pipeline trigger, and run monitoring
Tests use a test database and mock LLM responses to run deterministically without API costs
Each test starts with a clean database state using a beforeEach setup hook
Tests verify both UI state (element visibility, text content) and backend state (database records, file system)
The test suite runs in CI and reports results with screenshots on failure

userStories.title: Backend Integration Test Suite
userStories.description: As a developer, I want integration tests for all API routes so endpoint behavior is verified with realistic request/response cycles.
acceptanceCriteria: Integration tests use supertest to make HTTP requests to the Express app with an in-memory SQLite database
Test coverage includes: auth flow (register/login/refresh), spec CRUD, pipeline trigger/status, analytics endpoints, and team management
Each test file focuses on one route module and tests happy path, validation errors, auth failures, and edge cases
LLM calls are mocked using jest.mock to return deterministic responses without API costs
Tests verify response status codes, body structure, and database side effects

userStories.title: Performance Optimization: Database Indexes and Query Tuning
userStories.description: As a platform operator, I want optimized database queries and proper indexes so the API responds within performance targets even with large datasets.
acceptanceCriteria: Composite indexes are added for common query patterns: (workspace_id, status), (spec_id, created_at), (user_id, event_type)
The wal_events query used by SSE polling is optimized with a covering index on (workspace_id, id) with a WHERE clause on id > last_seen
Archive search query uses SQLite FTS5 (full-text search) for sub-100ms responses on specs with 10,000+ stories
An EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN audit verifies no full table scans exist for common API queries
Database query timing middleware logs queries taking longer than 100ms for monitoring

userStories.title: Production Deployment Checklist and Configuration
userStories.description: As a DevOps engineer, I want a production deployment configuration with all security, performance, and reliability settings so Rorcha can be deployed to production safely.
acceptanceCriteria: An nginx.conf template includes: HTTPS termination, gzip compression, static asset caching (1yr), API proxy with rate limiting, and security headers (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options)
Environment variable documentation lists all required and optional variables with defaults and security notes
A health check script verifies database connectivity, disk space, and process health for use with monitoring systems
Log rotation is configured for pipeline output logs and application logs using logrotate or equivalent
A DEPLOYMENT.md documents the step-by-step production setup process including SSL certificate, database migration, and backup configuration

userStories.title: Cancel Running Pipeline (Kill Switch)
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a cancel button on any running pipeline run so I can stop execution immediately without needing terminal access or manual DB fixes.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/pipeline/runs/:id/cancel sends SIGTERM to the run's PID and updates status to 'cancelled' with finished_at timestamp
If the process doesn't exit within 5s after SIGTERM, a SIGKILL is sent
Cancel button appears in the Pipeline Monitor for any run with status='running'
Button is replaced with a 'Cancelling...' spinner while the kill is in flight
After cancel, the terminal tab shows a [Run cancelled] message appended to the output
WAL event 'run_cancelled' is emitted on successful cancel
If PID is already dead, the endpoint still marks the run as cancelled and returns 200 (idempotent)

userStories.title: AI Direction Stack Wizard
userStories.description: As a non-technical user, I want a conversational wizard that interviews me about my project and automatically generates L1/L2/L3 direction layers so I never have to write YAML manually.
acceptanceCriteria: A 'Setup with AI' button appears on the Direction Stack panel when any layer is empty
Wizard asks 5-7 plain-English questions (project type, stack, key constraints, team size, deployment target)
Claude synthesizes answers into valid L1/L2/L3 YAML and shows a preview before saving
User can edit the preview before confirming — confirmed layers are saved via PUT /api/direction
Wizard can be re-run at any time to regenerate layers (with overwrite confirmation)
L3 output always satisfies the direction-validator schema (name, type, stack[], purpose, key_modules[])

userStories.title: Repo Auto-Scan for Direction Layer Proposals
userStories.description: As a developer adding an existing project, I want Rorcha to scan my repo structure and propose direction layer content automatically so setup takes seconds not minutes.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/workspaces/:id/scan-direction reads package.json, CLAUDE.md, README.md, and top-level directory structure from workspace.path
Claude generates draft L1/L2/L3 YAML from the scanned files
Response includes { l1Draft, l2Draft, l3Draft, confidence: 'low'|'medium'|'high' }
'Scan Repo' button appears in the Direction Stack panel and in the onboarding wizard
Drafts are shown in editable preview — never auto-saved without user confirmation
Scan completes in under 30s for repos under 500 files

userStories.title: Simple vs Advanced Direction Stack Toggle
userStories.description: As a new user, I want a simplified view of the direction stack that hides YAML and L1/L2/L3 terminology so I can configure AI context without understanding the underlying model.
acceptanceCriteria: Direction Stack panel has a 'Simple' / 'Advanced' toggle in the header (default: Simple for new workspaces, Advanced for existing)
Simple view shows plain-English summaries of each layer with Edit buttons that open a prose editor (no YAML)
Advanced view shows the current L1/L2/L3 tab editor unchanged
Switching from Simple to Advanced shows the raw YAML that was generated from prose
Switching from Advanced to Simple shows AI-summarized prose derived from the current YAML
Synthesized Output panel is always visible in both modes

userStories.title: Direction Stack Health Score
userStories.description: As a user, I want a health indicator on the Direction Stack panel that tells me in plain English what's configured, what's missing, and how it will affect spec quality.
acceptanceCriteria: Health score is computed client-side from layer content lengths and validation status
Score is displayed as a colored badge: Red (incomplete), Yellow (partial), Green (fully configured)
Tooltip or expandable section shows: which layers are empty, any validation errors, estimated impact on spec quality
Score updates live as layers are edited without requiring a save
Empty L1 shows warning: 'No global standards — specs will lack engineering guardrails'
Empty L3 shows warning: 'No project context — Claude won\'t know your stack or architecture'

userStories.title: LLM Provider Abstraction Layer
userStories.description: As a developer, I want llm-client.ts refactored into a multi-provider abstraction so Rorcha can route spec generation and story prompts through Anthropic SDK, OpenAI-compatible endpoints (any provider with a baseURL), or OpenRouter — determined by the user's configured provider and stored API key.
acceptanceCriteria: llm-client.ts exports a unified chatComplete(messages, opts) that accepts an optional provider override: 'anthropic' | 'openai-compat' | 'openrouter' | 'claude-cli' (default)
Provider 'anthropic' uses @anthropic-ai/sdk with the API key from BYOB vault or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY env var
Provider 'openai-compat' uses openai npm package with configurable baseURL and API key — covers OpenAI, Groq, Together, DeepSeek, Mistral, Ollama, and all Chinese labs
Provider 'openrouter' uses openai package with baseURL='https://openrouter.ai/api/v1' — covers Google Gemini, xAI Grok, and any other outlier
Provider 'claude-cli' retains existing claude --print subprocess path for users running on Claude subscription
Active provider and model are resolved in order: request param → workspace preferred_model → user BYOB key provider → DEFAULT_MODEL
TokenUsage is normalized across all providers to { inputTokens, outputTokens } regardless of SDK response shape
GET /api/direction/models returns available models filtered to the user's configured providers
Unit tests cover provider routing logic with mocked SDK responses
